title: In the Cold of the Night

facts.text: Director Nico Mastorakis shot this and the action film Hired to Kill back to back in 1990. Hired to Kill even name-checks this movie.
The film opens with Peggy Lee's 'Fever' over a fashion montage. The song began as a 1956 R&B No. 1 for Little Willie John, who reportedly disliked it at first.
Director Nico Mastorakis' back-to-back sister film Hired to Kill was shot mainly on the Greek island of Corfu, with Oliver Reed, George Kennedy and Brian Thompson.
Director Nico Mastorakis also made the notorious 1975 exploitation shocker Island of Death, and later co-created Greece's Star Channel in 1993.
Cinematographer Andreas Bellis also shot the notorious Swedish revenge film Thriller: A Cruel Picture (1973). Here he went for a softer, foggier look than that gritty work.
Director Nico Mastorakis' Zero Boys (1986) was among Hans Zimmer's earliest film scores, the first of four B-movies Zimmer scored for Mastorakis' Omega Entertainment in 1986-87.
The MPAA first slapped this film with an X rating, just before the NC-17 existed. It was cut to an R, and the full version later came out on video as NC-17.
Peggy Lee rewrote 'Fever' with new lyrics but never copyrighted them, so credit stayed with Eddie Cooley and Otis Blackwell, who used the pseudonym 'John Davenport' because of a contract.
Director Nico Mastorakis made his notorious Island of Death on Mykonos in 1975 for a reported $30,000. The UK banned it as a 'video nasty' from 1984 until 2011.
Director Nico Mastorakis said the MPAA's objection was to shots of Adrianne Sachs (Kimberly) on top of Jeff Lester (Scott) in the love scenes.
Republic Pictures Home Video released the film in both NC-17 and R versions in 1991. Both ran about 112 minutes, because the censorship trims were minimal.
Henry & June, the first NC-17 film, reportedly earned the rating partly from a Hokusai postcard of 'The Dream of the Fisherman's Wife' and a Paris ball scene. Sex on screen was newly risky.
The NC-17 rating had been created only months earlier, so this was among the first films to carry it. The first was Philip Kaufman's Henry & June.
Director Nico Mastorakis claims this film's X rating helped push studios to demand a new adults-only category. One blogger notes that's only his version of events.
David Soul (Dr. Frieberg) was Hutch on TV's Starsky & Hutch. His 1977 single 'Don't Give Up on Us' hit No. 1 on the US Hot 100 and in the UK.
Tippi Hedren (Clara) starred in Alfred Hitchcock's The Birds (1963). Her scene here includes a bird nod, and the film also references In the Heat of the Night and Friday the 13th.
Tippi Hedren (Clara) also made 1981's Roar with real lions and tigers. It took about 11 years, cost $17 million, grossed ~$2 million, and injured 70+ people, incl. her daughter Melanie Griffith.
Alfred Hitchcock discovered Tippi Hedren (Clara) in a TV commercial for a diet drink called Sego, then gave her a pricey two-day color screen test.
Adrianne Sachs (Kimberly) played the brunette prostitute in the famous 'Bitches leave!' scene of RoboCop (1987).
John Beck (shop owner Rudy) was in Woody Allen's Sleeper (1973) and played Moonpie opposite James Caan in sci-fi classic Rollerball (1975).
John Beck (Rudy) played Mark Graison in 67 episodes of TV's Dallas, and later voiced Frank Castle, the Punisher, in the 1990s Spider-Man animated series.
Adrianne Sachs was Miss Brazil in 1986 and appeared on the covers of more than 500 romance novels.
Star Jeff Lester (Scott Bruin) was earlier one of Bo Svenson's deputies in the 1981 TV spinoff of Walking Tall, and appeared in Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home.
Kimberly's laserdisc collection includes two other Nico Mastorakis films, The Wind (1986) and Glitch! (1988). A little self-promotion from the director.
Marc Singer (Ken Strom) voiced Man-Bat on Batman: The Animated Series, and played Matt Cantrell in Dallas' ninth 'dream season'.
Vanity Fair called Shannon Tweed (Lena) 'one of home video's most rented erotic thriller goddesses.' She has appeared in over 60 films, including Night Eyes 2 and 3.
Star Jeff Lester (Scott Bruin) is married to singer-actress Susan Anton. He later quit acting to direct commercials and music videos.
Mondo Digital's reviewer calls this a near-perfect example of mainstream erotic thrillers from before Basic Instinct, praising its over-the-top style and camp appeal.
Blogger Fred Barrett says the film's nightmare sequences look like LaserDisc-era video graphics. He ties it to Looker (1981), Videodrome (1983) and Brian De Palma's thrillers.
Shannon Tweed (Lena) was Playboy's 1982 Playmate of the Year. She is married to KISS bassist Gene Simmons, and the two starred in the reality show Gene Simmons Family Jewels.
Brian Thompson (Phil) later played Klingon Lt. Klag on Star Trek: The Next Generation, the Klingon who says 'Gagh is always best when served live.'
David Soul (Dr. Frieberg) first got national attention as the masked 'Covered Man' singing on The Merv Griffin Show. On Top Gear he posted a fast lap but broke the car's gearbox.
Brian Thompson (Phil) was the Night Slasher in Cobra (1986) and a Terminator-era punk in The Terminator (1984). He was also once Nico Mastorakis' son-in-law.
Rob Hunter of Film School Rejects called the film ridiculous but said its softcore fun and stellar B-movie cast outweigh the moments that overstay their welcome.
Brian Orndorf of Blu-ray.com called the film 'ridiculous' too, saying it labors through an uninteresting story with an 'uncomfortably dim protagonist.'
Marc Singer (Ken Strom) is best known as The Beastmaster (1982) and as Mike Donovan in the TV series V. He has a black belt in kung fu.
Jack Kehler, the homeless man here, didn't act until age 24, made his film debut in Strange Invaders (1983), and later recurred on The Man in the High Castle.
Marc Singer (Ken Strom) made his early mark as a gladiator on the Planet of the Apes TV series, and was cast as Andy Warner in Roots: The Next Generations.
The director's own red Chevy was used as a picture car. During a car stunt it nearly blew a gasket.
Though mostly a straight-to-video release in the US, the film also got theatrical runs in Japan, Portugal and South Korea.
The Good Efficient Butchery blog calls this a mix of a late-'80s Italian fashion giallo and an early direct-to-video erotic thriller, anticipating the VR craze of The Lawnmower Man.
Locations include Venice's Muscle Beach, the Third Street Tunnel downtown and Pacific Coast Highway in Malibu.
The 2nd Street Tunnel, a location here, also appears in Blade Runner, The Terminator, Flashdance, Lethal Weapon 2, Demolition Man and Con Air.
Vinegar Syndrome restored the film in 4K from its original 35mm camera negative for a 2019 Blu-ray release.
Peggy Lee's 'Fever' and The Lettermen's 'Love Is a Many Splendored Thing' are on the soundtrack alongside John Cameron's 'Scott's Theme'.
Peggy Lee's 'Fever' peaked at No. 8 on the Billboard chart in July 1958, her biggest hit. Its stripped-down arrangement is just bass, percussion, finger snaps and voice.
Jack Kehler, who plays the homeless man, is also known as the Dude's landlord in The Big Lebowski.
Shannon Tweed (Lena) lived at the Playboy Mansion about 14 months as Hugh Hefner's partner and met Gene Simmons there. She later voiced a character on SpongeBob SquarePants.
Brian Thompson (Phil) later played the villain Shao Kahn in Mortal Kombat: Annihilation (1997) and the Alien Bounty Hunter on The X-Files.
